chunks: Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The liar is destroyed by the evidences, and his followers are destroyed by the doubts.'
ai.seo_question: How are liars and their followers destroyed differently according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the epistemological roots of spiritual ruin, distinguishing between the liar who is defeated by objective evidence (bayyinat) and his followers who succumb to subjective ambiguity (shubahat). This distinction reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the clarity of the Imam's truth versus the deceptive subtleties of false narratives, illustrating how different audiences are led astray through distinct cognitive mechanisms.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The liar gets destroyed by the evidences and his followers get destroyed by the doubts’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn al-Hakam has narrated (from Aban) from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following: “

I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘A liar is destroyed by means of clear evidence (his false claims) and his followers are destroyed on ambiguous evidence (accepting a leader whose qualification is doubtful).”’
